system_scope.summary: An event framework where the application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent; the Main module is part of the framework; the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers; it includes an Event Queue and a base Handler extended by standard and application-specific handlers.

business_drivers.statement: Provide an Event framework to be used by an application.
Handle and process events through component interaction.
Allow application components to utilize the framework services.
Must handle system termination via STOP handler.
Must maintain system in idle state until input is received.

architecture_evidence.statement: An Event framework where the application logic and framework are highly inter-dependent.
The Main module is part of the framework.
The Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers.
It features a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers.
Fully developed architecture with class diagrams, component descriptions, and defined component interactions.
System accepts input via Command Line Interface (CLI).
Single processor execution implied (sequential event processing).
Events must be dispatched in a First-Come-First-Served (FIFO) pattern.
System must maintain an 'idle wait' state until input is received.
Application logic is embedded within framework components.
performance_proxy: Number of components involved in a transaction.
transaction_speed: Qualitative (Slow due to high number of components involved).
Evaluators probe the Event-Driven Architecture style.
Evaluators ask whether the system allows unauthorized access, portrays data confidentiality, and processes any task in the fastest possible speed.

open_questions.question: Can the components of the architecture be reused for future projects?
Can the framework be expanded in the future to accommodate a new application or new components?
Will the system handle any input given by the user and handle invalid input?
Is the architecture consistent in behavior?
Can any new application-specific functionality be added to the architecture?
Can the system be modified in short time and cost-effective manner?
Does the architecture perform its event-processing task properly?
How is unauthorized access prevented, and what security controls support confidentiality?
What measurable performance expectations define 'fastest possible speed'?
Which components own invalid-input handling and recovery behavior?
